entries.x: The app has four tabs: Events, Collection, Insights and Account. Events is the product: players and organizers arrive there to play or run a tournament. Collection holds the Library: every card you own, your binders and wants, your decks, your cubes and your trades. Insights shows the metagame and Arena draft data. Account holds your profile, friends and sharing.
A live card for the event you're in, invitations, upcoming events, and past events tucked away. + New creates an event; Life opens the life tracker for the match you're playing, or a local one.

Your collection's hero art with its card count and value (tap for All cards), then rows of your Decks, Binders and Cubes to swipe through. + adds cards or makes a deck, binder or cube; the magnifier searches every card; the camera scans a pile of cards to add anywhere. Trade, Wants and Import sit along the bottom.
(what's winning in Standard, Pioneer, Modern, Legacy, Vintage, Pauper and Canadian Highlander) or Limited (the sets on Arena), each opening with a short written summary.
Your avatar and record, Friends, Sharing, View your profile, settings such as how you track games, privacy switches, notices from Table 1, and account deletion.

The tab bar runs along the bottom (on the website on a phone too): an icon over each tab's name, the tab you're on in white under a thin teal line, the others with icon and name in the same light grey. It shows only on those four screens. Every screen you open from them has a back arrow on the left, and on iPhone a swipe from the left edge goes back too (the camera is the exception).

(Limited): pick a set from a searchable list with set icons, or a cube. Your cubes from the Library come first, then recent cubes; or paste a Cube Cobra link and the name fills in. Picking a cube hides the link and name fields. A roto draws its card pool from the Library cube you pick.
(team formats): 3 or 4 players per team.

(Draft): Auto (pods of up to 8) or Choose 1 to 16, never so many that a pod would have fewer than 2; the line under it says how they split for the players so far ("2 pods · 9, 8"). Pairings: Inside pods (after round 1 you play your own pod; new drafts start here) or Across pods (Swiss over everyone). Automatic rounds count the largest pod inside pods ("Auto · 3 rounds for pods of 9"), everyone across. Team drafts and rotos are one pod.

(Swiss events, on to start): the number of rounds follows the players signed up, "Auto · 4 rounds for 12 players": 2 players play 1 round, 3–4 play 2, 5–8 play 3, 9–16 play 4, 17–32 play 5, 33–64 play 6, 65–128 play 7, and bigger events follow the Magic Tournament Rules' table. It's fixed when round 1 is paired. Switch it off to set the rounds by hand.
(Swiss events of players): No top cut or Top 8. Top 8 needs 9 or more players; with fewer the event ends after Swiss.
(Constructed): Off, Optional or Required. Players add theirs as text or from their own Table 1 decks; Required holds round 1 until every list is in.
(set by hand, team events and roto): 1 to 15, default 3. Rounds run 50 minutes. A switch shows or hides the clock everywhere for that event; results still auto-confirm at round end either way.
(roto): Round robin for 2 to 8 players, Swiss for 9 or more, changeable until round 1. Round robin sets the number of rounds itself.

Nearby + QR (players within 150 m can find and join it, and nearby players with alerts on are told) or QR only; an event that starts now is pinned where you stand. (drafts): one long table per pod, drawn upright, seats running clockwise. Seat the ends (4+ players) puts seat 1 at the head and one at the foot. The middle reads "↻ 1·3 left" and "↺ 2 right"; see who you face in round 1.

(Seating, drafts): the same Pods and Pairings rows as Create, saved at once (a new number of pods re-draws the seats). Randomize draws every pod and seat again. Tap a seat to Move to another pod (to its end) or a new pod, or Swap with… and tap the other player; seats close up so every pod stays 1 to n, and every move is logged. Players who join after the draw are listed as "Not seated" and go to the smallest pod at round 1, leaving your arrangement alone. Each pod's note names its left-over seat: "Seat 7 plays Pod 2's seat 7", or "Seat 7 has the bye" when the event is odd. Locked once round 1 is paired.
(team events): randomize, move players, rename teams.

a tab after Round with every earlier round, newest first; tap a match to correct its result.

(More; the bar on the website): pairs the running round again from the standings as they are now, with a fresh clock. It asks first and says when results already in will be cleared. A notice on the Round tab offers it when an earlier result was corrected after the round was paired ("A round 2 result changed after round 3 was paired."). Only the latest round, while it runs, with no open dispute in earlier rounds; the old pairings stay in the event's log, and players are told "Round 3 re-paired".

after the last Swiss round the button is Cut to top 8 (it asks first), which pairs the quarterfinals by Swiss standings: 1 v 8, 4 v 5, 2 v 7, 3 v 6, the higher seed choosing to play or draw. Then Pair semifinals, Pair the final and Finish event. Playoff matches need a winner: draws can't be entered. Rounds are named Quarterfinals, Semifinals and Final, and the standings gain a Top 8 bracket with each seed and score.

in a team event with two teams, once one team has more match wins than the other could reach with every match still to play (5 of 9 in a 3-on-3 over three rounds, 7 of 12 in a 4-on-4), the round shows "Team Alpha has clinched it: 5–1 in match wins with 3 matches left to play" and the big button is Finish event straight away. Matches not yet played don't count for anyone. If the round is in, Play on · pair round N keeps going instead. A dispute still has to be settled first.

A winner card (or winning team) above the final standings. With a top 8 the order is the winner, the finalist, the semifinalists, the quarterfinalists (each by seed), then everyone else by their Swiss standing.
Every round's matches, newest first. Results can still be corrected; standings and records update.
Cancelled events show standings after the last completed round and the reason.
One player's report counts. If the opponent reports the same score it's confirmed; a different score is a dispute.
Results auto-confirm at round end. Disputes must be settled before the next round can be paired.
The organizer can set any result; every change is recorded. A correction made after the next round was paired can be followed by Re-pair on that round.

Scoring follows the Magic Tournament Rules: 3 points for a win, 1 for a draw, a bye counts as a win; tiebreakers are opponents' match-win %, game-win % and opponents' game-win %, each with a 33% floor.

round 1 is across each table; odd pods' last seats play each other, pod 1's against pod 2's, and only an odd event has a bye. Inside pods, later rounds pair each pod by its own standings; an odd pod's lowest-ranked player (one who can cross without a rematch) plays another pod's, and the bye, if any, goes to one of them who hasn't had one. Across pods, later rounds are ordinary Swiss. Standings are one list either way, and the top 8 cuts from it.

Team events: a team wins a round by winning more of its matches; teams are ordered by those round results, then total match wins. Inside each team, players are listed best first by record, then game-win %, then opponents' match-win %, each with their record ("2-0").
Older app versions still run these events, but show Finish where newer ones show Cut to top 8. The organizer's match and guest scorekeeping are on iOS; Seat the ends on iOS, Android and the website.
The Events tab's live card shows your table, opponent and round clock, and leads with reporting your result (or opening the life tracker, if you chose that in settings).
Report a match in one tap; your opponent confirms or disputes it.

before round 1 an event's link (table-1.site/s/…) shows when and where it is, the format, who runs it, the rounds ("Auto rounds · Top 8"), how many have signed up ("12/16 players · 3 on the waitlist") and Sign up. Signed out, Sign up goes through sign-in (Apple, Google or email, which make an account if you don't have one) and comes back signed up, in the app or on the website. A full event offers Join the waitlist, then says your place ("You're number 2 on the waitlist"); when a place opens you're seated and get a "You're in" notification. Private events don't show.
until round 1, leave your seat or your place on the waitlist from the event screen; the next person on the waitlist moves up.

(Constructed events that take them): the Decklist row on the event screen ("Add your decklist", or "Required · add it before round 1"; Events says "Add your decklist" too while it's missing). Paste it as text (Arena, MTGO and Moxfield lists all read, and the screen counts "60 main · 15 sideboard" as you go) or pick one of your own decks in the event's format. Change or remove it until round 1; after that ask the organizer. Only you and the organizer see it.
the same link shows Standings (with the top 8 bracket once there is one) and Matchups: every round's tables and scores, newest first. Anyone with the link can follow along, signed in or not.

(iPhone and Android Events tab, under Scan QR and Nearby; the website's box on its home page): type the organizer's 4-character code and Join, or Paste what you copied (a code, a join link, the QR's link, or a message with the code in it) and it joins at once. A wrong, closed or full event says so under the box.

Join by QR, link, code or nearby. A join link (with or without the QR's secret) opens the app and joins when the app is installed, and the website otherwise. A nearby event you've already joined (or run) says Joined and opens the event instead of offering Join.

Scan the organizer's QR with your phone's camera. Signed out, the page (or the app, if you have it) names the event you're joining (its name, format, venue, organizer and how many players are in) and offers Continue with Apple, Google or email. Each one makes your account if you don't have one; a new email account adds your first and last name, and then you're seated. On the website you can also join as a guest with just a name. Private events show only their code until you're in.

after joining on a phone's browser, the event screen offers the app for that phone and says which sign-in to use there ("Continue with Apple", or the email address). Your seat is on your account, so signing in the same way puts the event on the app's Events tab. On Android the store link also carries the event through the install: the app opens on it the first time (after you sign in). Not now hides it on that browser. Guests don't see it (their seat lives in that browser).
Before you join, the app says plainly that your name shows in the event's pairings and standings, to its players and anyone with its standings link.

Standings and matchups are public by link, so friends can follow along. A code join to a full event puts you on the waitlist (guests are told it's full); the QR and nearby joins say it's full, since the organizer can add you.
In a top 8, your playoff rounds are named Quarterfinals, Semifinals and Final, and can't be reported as a draw.

On iPhone, the round shows in a Live Activity and widgets (the round clock, your table and your opponent on the Lock Screen; results go in from the app), and push notifications tell you when you're paired.
In drafts you see your seat at the table and the pass direction for each pack; in team events your team and seat letter.

photograph your own deck (or pick a photo) with a note. Before saving, Rotate left or Rotate right turns it upright. Only you and the organizer see it until the event is over. On iPhone, Android and the website, when you're signed in; a guest's deck can be added by the organizer.

(signed in, in the apps): its link opens the event page in the app, never the website: the sign-up page before round 1, then Standings | Matchups (top 8, teams and pods included; every round's tables and scores), refreshing every 20 seconds. Its notifications open the same page.

on that page, for anyone signed in who isn't its organizer or a player (and can see it by its link). It's listed on the Events tab under Following (running first, then upcoming, then finished in the last week), with a notification when each round is paired, when it finishes and if it's cancelled. Following → turn notifications off, or Unfollow. Up to 200; nobody sees who follows.

On the website, the event screen has a back arrow to Events (or wherever you came from). So does the event's shared link page (sign-up, standings and matchups, signed in or out): opened straight from a link, the arrow goes to the home page.

One line says what's next: "Waiting on 3 results", then Ready: Pair round 4 or Ready: Finish event once every result is in. Under it: disputes to decide, and guest matches you have to enter yourself.
Between rounds it says "Round 3 recorded · Pair round 4". It ends with the event.
You get an alert when a match is disputed and when the last result of a round comes in, not for every result.
It only shows: pairing and deciding disputes happen on the organizer screen, one tap away. If you also play, your own match has its own Live Activity as before.
A home screen widget (small or medium) and a Lock Screen one: your next event's format, name, venue and player count, and when it starts ("In 2h 10m", or the day and time).
A live event comes first, then the soonest one with a start time. It says when you're organizing. The medium size adds the one after and any invitations waiting.
It uses what the Events tab shows, refreshed when you open the app and every so often in between.
A home screen widget: your collection's value in USD, the change over the last 7 days, and a line of the last 30 days. The medium size adds distinct cards and copies.
The change counts cards you added or removed as well as price moves, so it says "7 days", not "market".
It starts tracking when you add it, so the first day shows just the value ("From today").
Kept off the Lock Screen, and hidden while your phone is locked, because your collection's value is private.

(iPhone small; Android one cell, resizable to any shape): the card's art filling the widget under a 60% dark scrim, with the Table 1 mark in white at the app icon's size. No words. A tap opens Table 1 where you left it, as the icon does. With no card picked, or its art missing, it's the plain icon.

the phone keeps the last 12 you picked, newest first; picking one again moves it up. Each widget shows the newest unless you pick one in its settings (iPhone: Edit Widget → Card; Android: Newest or a card, with its art). A widget whose card was removed goes back to the newest.
Kept on the phone, not in your account, so they stay through sign-out and don't follow you to another device. The website has no widgets.

each has its own settings (iPhone: long-press → Edit Widget; Android: the settings screen that opens when you place it on older Android, or the widget's settings or Reconfigure on newer ones): Format (Standard, Pioneer, Modern, Legacy, Vintage, Pauper, Canadian Highlander), Events (Big events or All events) and Window (7, 14, 30 or 90 days). They start on Modern, Big events, 30 days. When Big events has nothing in the window, the widget shows All events and says so on its label.

(iPhone small, medium, large; Android any size): "MODERN · BIG · 30D", a bar of the whole meta with each archetype in its color, and the most played archetypes with their shares (five, or eight on the large size). From the medium size up, the graph: Meta over time for those archetypes across the window, each line in its color. The large size adds each archetype's change on the window before (▲ in teal, ▼ in pink) and its win rate.

(iPhone medium, large; Android two rows and up): the window's matchup grid, the most played archetypes along the top (by short initials, over a line in their color) against the rows that fit, each square's win rate tinted teal or pink like the Insights tab, faded under 30 matches.

(iPhone small, medium, large; Android any size): pick the archetype in the widget's settings (the format's archetypes, those with matchups first; or leave it on the most played). It shows the archetype's win rate and share; small adds its best and worst matchup, medium Good against and Bad against (three each, from 20 or more decided matches), large every matchup as a bar from 50%, with its percent and match count.

the eight most played archetypes of the window each get their own color (a palette checked for color-blind readers on Table 1's dark background), the rest grey; an archetype has the same color in all three widgets with the same settings, and its name always sits beside it.

on the Matchup grid: it's outlined, its row and column names light up, and the top line reads "Broodscale Combo vs Izzet Prowess" with the record ("321-236-14"); large adds the win rate and likely range, or "Only 2 matches: too few to say". Tap it again to let go, or another square to move. On iPhone, two grid widgets with the same settings share what's tapped.
in Meta's list (medium and up): its line is drawn on top and the other lines and decks fade. Tap again to let go.
(iPhone): decks in white that fades by place, winning squares filled faintly, losing ones outlined, text always full, so every number stays readable.

A tap anywhere else opens Insights on the same format, events and window (the grid, or the archetype's page). The widgets read the same public Insights data as the tab, with no sign-in, and refresh every three hours; offline before their first load they say the format loads when you're online.

a Limited set's best cards in draft (Premier draft when the set has it; all players): place, color dots, name, rarity letter, points above or below the set's average win rate, and the sort's number in teal. The Set, Rarity and Color buttons and the sort's code across the top, "Data from 17Lands" at the bottom.

three small boxed buttons across the top. Set (its code) steps through the Limited sets Insights has, round to the first; Rarity steps Any → Common → Uncommon → Rare → Mythic → Any (hidden for an Arena cube, which has none); Color steps Any (five dots) → White → Blue → Black → Red → Green → Multicolor → Colorless → Any. One choice at a time; several rarities or colors from the settings go to Any on the next tap. The cards change at once, a new set's after its cards are fetched. Small widgets use letters ("All", "U", "C·U"), the large one words ("Any rarity", "Uncommon"). On iPhone the buttons' picks belong to the widget's settings: editing them starts over, and two widgets with the same settings share them. On Android they're the widget's own picks, so its settings screen shows them.

Set (the Limited sets in Insights), Sort (win rate in hand, in the opening hand, improvement when drawn, average pick), and Rarity and Color, several of each, none picked meaning all (iPhone: Edit Widget; Android: its settings screen). With no set picked it shows the newest set the phone knows.

iPhone small (4 cards), medium (6) and large (12); Android any size from 2×1, rows filling the height (up to 12), the one-row strip showing the set and the best card.

A tap anywhere but a button opens Insights → Limited on that set with the widget's sort, rarity and color picked (a widget from before this update opens on the set alone). The set list comes from Insights (signed in, or what the app kept the last time Insights → Limited was opened); the cards need no sign-in and refresh every six hours, and offline the widget keeps its last answer.

for each event you play in or run, in its own quiet Live events group (alerts still come as ordinary notifications). Playing: "T3 · vs Ana" with the round ("R2/4") and the round clock counting down, and no result buttons, ranks or records (results go in from the app; a bye or waiting shows that line instead). Running: "5/8 in" with a bar, the next step, disputes and results to enter yourself, and the clock. A tap opens the event. When the event ends the last line stays half an hour, then goes. Next event, Collection value and Current match, drawn like the iPhone's (same labels, order, colors and buttons) with the same rules. Current match ticks the round clock and, from the wider size, reports (2-0 to 0-2), confirms or disputes without opening the app. Android has no lock screen widgets; the live notification covers the match there.

long-press a widget and drag its edges, from one row up to the full width and any height. One row: Next event shows when and the name, Collection value the amount (wide: with the line and the week's change), Current match the round, table and clock. 2×2 and 4×2 are the iPhone's small and medium. Three rows and up: Next event lists the later events that fit under the first (tap one to open it, "+2 more" for the rest), Collection value grows the amount and the 30-day line, and Current match shows the big clock, where the result stands and all five result buttons (on a narrow one, Confirm above Dispute).
and long-press shortcuts on the app icon: Life tracker and Scan cards.

The app refreshes them whenever it reads your events, when it comes back to the front, and when a notification about an event arrives. A widget fetches for itself when its copy is old (Next event 15 minutes, Collection value 6 hours, Current match 5 minutes). Signing out clears them.

A rotisserie draft: the whole cube is laid out face up and players take turns picking from it, snake order by seat. The picks fill a deck in each player's Library, then rounds run like any other event.
Pick one of your Library cubes (a Cube Cobra link is imported first). The cube must hold players × picks.
Picks per player (default 45), order (Snake or Same order), and an optional pick clock that can change by round (30 s to 24 h), pause and resume.
seats everyone at random. Pick for anyone, or Undo last pick.
A summary line on top: who's on the clock, the pick number, and "You pick in 3" or Your pick.
(seats × rounds), Cube (by color, Available / All / Picked), Picks (anyone's, with colors and curve) and My list.
My list is a private ranked list; with Auto-pick on, your turn picks the top card still there. Taken cards leave everyone's list at once.
Your deck is a normal Library deck marked "From <event>". It never counts as Missing.
Round robin or Swiss, then results and standings as usual.
A guest who claims their seat later gets the deck at once.
If someone picked that card first, you see it taken and pick again.

(all platforms): once the event is over, everyone in it sees every deck photo and its note, and players can still add theirs: Deck photos · Add under After the event, or More → Add a deck photo on the organizer's Results. The player or whoever took it can edit the note, remove it, or Rotate right / Rotate left to set a sideways photo upright; it turns for everyone and the original file stays as it was. Photos show whole, not cropped. Hold a photo for Copy, Save to Photos and Share, on the event's screen and on your account: the photo upright as shown (iPhone: the phone's own menu; website: the browser's picture menu, or right-click; Android: a Table 1 menu).

Account → Deck photos ("12 photos · 5 events", under your lifetime record) lists every photo of a deck you played across events, whoever took it, headed by event (name, format, date), newest event first. Each photo's menu: Open event, Everyone's photos from this event (finished events), Rotate, the note and Remove. On all three; the website at table-1.site/me/deck-photos.

(finished set drafts, iPhone, Android and the website ): everyone in the event scans their cards into one pile, most valuable first, with who added each card and its market price, and the pile's total. Tap a card to take it out. The website has no camera scanner, so there cards are added by search, in the drafted set's printing when the card is in it, with a Foil switch.

Full screen, edge to edge, screen stays awake. With two players, your half is at the bottom and your opponent's is upside down at the top; with three to five, everyone sits around the phone. Tap the top of a number for +1, the bottom for −1; hold to repeat.

Opened without an event (from Events, the life tracker shortcut or a tracker link), the tracker starts on Setup: Players 2 · 3 · 4 · 5 and Starting life 20 · 30 · 40, starting on what you picked last time.
begins a fresh game and opens the Chooser, so the table picks who goes first.
(when a saved game has changes or recorded games) picks it up where you left it.
in Options or History goes back to Setup. An event's match never shows Setup: it's always two players at the event's life.

Players sit clockwise from the bottom, each facing their own edge of the phone: three is one down each side and one at the bottom, four is two down each side, five is two down each side and one at the bottom. They're named P1 to P5 (two players stay You and Opponent).

Each seat works like a two-player half, the way its player sees it: life on their left, counters beside it, +1 on their top half, and a swipe toward themselves to open the counter picker (only Done closes it).

lights up once only one player is left and is filled in with them; otherwise it asks who won, listing every player and Draw. Games follow one another with no best of three, and History keeps the score ("P1 1 · P2 0 · P3 2").

At 30 or 40 starting life (Commander 40, Pauper Commander 30), the counter picker lists commander damage from each opponent first ("Commander P3", or just "Commander" with one opponent), then poison and the rest. A turned-on column reads "Cmd P3".
Commander damage is life lost too: +1 takes a life, −1 gives it back, and Undo or Reset takes both back together. History shows it ("P1 · Commander P3 +3 → 3").
commander damage from one opponent loses the game; that column turns red. Oathbreaker plays at 20 without commander damage.
A tap counts the moment your finger touches down; if it turns into a swipe, the change is taken back.

Swipe down on a half to turn on up to 3 counters: poison (you lose at 10), energy, experience, rad and speed (and commander damage at 30+ life). Done closes the picker: no swipe does, so swiping up scrolls its list instead of closing it.
The center strip shows the round clock (teal, amber under 10 minutes, pink in overtime), your round and table, and Record · Options · Reset. Someone watching sees Options only.

asks first, then puts everyone's life back to the starting life and every counter to 0 for this game. In a game on your own phone with games already recorded, it also offers Reset match, which clears the games too and keeps the players, starting life and counters you turned on. In an event, recorded games stay: they're the event's record.
rises from the bottom: Chooser, Roll dice, History, New match (without an event) and Leave tracker.

covers the screen. Everyone puts a finger down; a ring closes around each finger, and once no finger has landed or lifted for two seconds one is picked at random and fills in teal. A moment later (1.5 seconds) the tracker comes back on its own; Done leaves sooner.

pick the die (D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20) and how many (1 to 10), then Roll. The total shows large, with each die under it ("2D6 · 4 + 5"); tap the total to roll again. Your die and count are remembered.
History groups quick taps into one entry ("Marcus · Life −5 → 15") and lets you undo.

With two players, when someone hits 0 life or 10 poison Record lights up. Recording a game moves to the next one; when the match is decided the app offers to report it, for example "Report 2–1 to the event?".
In an event, both players' phones stay in sync and the organizer can watch read-only (or keep score for a guest match).

What's winning, at a glance. Its own tab between Collection and Account (in the sidebar on a computer), with Constructed | Limited at the top; the app remembers which you used last. Free for anyone signed in.

Pick Standard, Pioneer, Modern, Legacy, Vintage, Pauper or Canadian Highlander, Big events or All events, and a window of 7, 14, 30 or 90 days (30 to start), from dropdowns: one row of three cells (Format · Events · Window) with a small arrow, each opening its list with the current choice outlined. The format list ends in Shown formats…, which opens the switches that hide formats you don't play. A list's own screen (Meta now and the rest) has the Events and Window dropdowns it needs.

Meta over time and the matchup grid come first, then In brief with the Decks · Events · Through numbers, then one row each for Meta now, Cards rising and falling, New set, Bans and unbans (Points changes in Canadian Highlander) and Big events (or Events). Each row sums its list up in one line ("Eldrazi Bloodchief Combo 17% · 25 archetypes", "Rising most: Lightning Bolt ▲ 11", "24 events · latest Modern Challenge 64") and opens it on its own screen, in full, with the pickers that list depends on; they're the same picks as the format page.

each deck's share of top finishes and its change from the window before, and under it "Win 54.2% · Conv 31% · 1st 16%": its win rate in matches against other decks (top 8 brackets and paper rounds; mirrors left out, draws count as not won; shown from 20 matches), its conversion rate (the share of its lists that made top 8, in events with a top 8, leagues left out; shown from 20 lists; on Magic Online only the top 32 lists are published, so there it's top 32 to top 8), and 1st, the share of the window's events it won.

every named deck with at least 1% of the window's decks (as well as the eight biggest), its share day by day over the window you picked (7, 14, 30 or 90 days), with bans and new sets marked. Shorter windows show dates along the bottom, 90 days shows months; a deck with no results in the window drops off the chart. The chart runs the full width: tap a deck in the row under it to light up its line, and that deck's button shows its current share. A set is marked only when it brings the format new cards, so reprint sets like Mystery Booster Commander don't show.
the cards played more and less (main deck or sideboard), and the newest set's cards ranked by how much they're played.
for each ban or unban in the last year, the decks it hit, the decks that gained, what took the banned cards' place, and how long the meta took to settle.

right under Meta over time: each row's win rate against each column, the columns the ten most played decks named along the top, and a row for every named deck with at least 1% of the decks and 20 matches, plus Other at the bottom. It follows the Big events / All events and window you picked ("Matchups · All events, last 30 days"). A pairing with fewer than 30 matches is faded: a hint, not a verdict. Tap a square for that matchup's record, shown below the grid. Overall, the first column, is each row's win rate against every archetype in the window (its Meta now record, or the sum of its squares when the window has none), colored like a square; tap it for "Broodscale Combo overall" with the record and its likely range. On a phone it scrolls in its own box, the deck names pinned on the left and the column names on top.

signed in, the grid's rows start with the archetypes you have a deck of in that format ("Your deck", or "Your 2 decks"), then those whose usual list your collection covers at 60% or more ("You have 84%", most first; the usual list is every card in at least half that archetype's lists, at its usual copies, basic lands left out), then the rest in their usual order.
The last month's big events with their top 8s.

Tap a deck for its share over time, record, an example list (its best recent finish at the biggest event) with Add to my decks, core and flex cards, sideboard, matchups and recent finishes with full lists. Other is broken down by colors instead, each group with its share and an example list. Tap a card for its card page (below).

the search icon at the top of Constructed opens "<Format> cards". From two letters it lists the cards played in that format in the last year, never a basic land: the exact name first, then names starting with what you typed or with a word starting with it, then anywhere in the name, then close spellings, each by how much it was played in the last 90 days, with "Main 23% · Side 0.5%" (or "Not in the last 90 days · 6 lists this year"). Nothing found says "No Modern lists played a card called that this year."

(from search, Cards rising and falling, or a ban study) follows the format page's Big events / All events and window, with the pickers on the page: Main · Side · Copies (copies: the average in lists that main it), Lists ("235/707"), first and last seen; Share of lists by week over a year, main and sideboard, marked where the card itself was banned, unbanned, restricted or given new points; Played in: every archetype with a list playing it, a bar of how many of its lists do ("108 of 112 lists · 3.7 main · 1.0 side"), tapping through to the archetype; and Best lists: the ten best lists that played it in the window (biggest events, then best finish, then newest), "1st · Modern Challenge 64" and "Burn · 4 main · 1 side · NOV 3", each opening the full list with Add to my decks. Open the card goes to its own page with prices and your copies.

opens like a deck shared with you: card art, grouped by type, View (list, grid, stacks, Group by, Sort), search, Export and Deck image, with Add to my decks on top and where it finished above. Tap a card for its card page.

at the end of the format row hides the formats you don't play (one always stays). Your picks follow your account: hidden formats and sets, and the format, events, window, set, event and players you picked, open the same way on every device.
has Points changes where other formats have bans: each points update is marked POINTS on the charts, with a page for who it hit and who gained.

Pick a set on Arena, or an Arena cube run, shown by its name, such as Arena Powered Cube · Oct 2025, the event (Premier, Traditional, Pick Two or Sealed, where there's data), and All players or Top players (a 60% win rate or better over 50 games), from the Set · Event · Players dropdowns (Event and Players only when there's a choice; the set list ends in Shown sets… to hide sets you don't draft).

Top cards leads the page, with Sort (win rate in hand, in the opening hand, improvement when drawn, average pick), Rarity (not for a cube) and Color (W U B R G, Multicolor, Colorless) dropdowns, each taking several picks (the list stays open; a tap puts an option in or out, Any clears, Done closes; the cell reads "C · U" or "WU · Multi"), a search box, and the ten best cards for them. Each row: its place, the art of the set's own printing, the name, the mana cost in Scryfall's symbols, rarity and games in hand, and the sort's number with, for the win rates, the points above or below the format's average under it ("+4.1"). Show all N opens the rest. Art and mana costs come from the card file on your device (the page fetches it if it's missing).

two letters or more find the set's cards by name (starts first, accents and apostrophes ignored), whatever the filters. With no match in the set, it searches every other set's draft data on the device, up to 20, under "Not in <set> · in other sets", and a tap opens the card's page in that set.
a card is kept when all its colors are picked, so White + Blue keeps white, blue and Azorius gold cards; Multicolor keeps every gold card, Colorless the colorless ones.

After the cards: the color pairs and the rest, In brief and Games · Average · Weeks, New in Insights, and at the very bottom Rank this set, the page's big action, with who has ranked it under the words, then New sets to rank.
opens on the card's picture in the set's printing and its mana cost, then its win rates.
against the set's average, Deck colors (every main-color combination with its splash), and pairs week by week: the chart's scale fits the win rates shown, with the average as a dashed AVG line.

win rate in hand, in the opening hand, the gain from drawing it, and how early it's taken, with rarity and color filters (a cube has no rarities, so no rarity filter). Taken vs win rate shows which cards go later than they should.
on the play and on the draw, mulligans, game length.
(Rank this cube for a cube run) opens its Rankings, and New sets to rank lists sets with no 17Lands data yet ("Out Nov 13 · 286 cards").

a set still to come, or out in the last four weeks, with no 17Lands data yet leads the set row by its code (TRK for Star Trek). Picking it says when it's out, that draft data follows about three weeks after a set reaches Arena (some never do), and how many cards Scryfall has so far, with Rank this set and the New in Insights switch. The row still opens on the newest set with data. Shown sets… lists them with the other sets, so they can be hidden the same way. The row draws once it knows which sets are coming, which it remembers on your device after your first visit, so they never jump in at the front a moment later.

each cube Arena runs (Powered, Arena Cube, Planar, and any other 17Lands adds) gets an entry per run, named by its month ("Arena Powered Cube · Oct 2025"), with weeks counted from that run's first draft. A later run is a new entry; the old one stays as it was.

(at the bottom of Limited): a notification when a new Constructed format, a set's first draft data, a new cube run, or a set ready to rank (within 10 days of release) arrives. Once each, to people who opened Insights in the last 60 days; the switch turns it off.

Constructed: published Magic Online results (Challenges, Qualifiers, Showcases and Leagues), plus paper events of 32 or more players from TopDeck.gg and from Melee.gg, a year back. Bigger events count for more: 128 or more players four times a regular event, 64 or more twice, Regional Championships and other championships four times at any size, and a top 8 finish double.

events come from MTG_decklistcache, an open collection of tournament results kept on GitHub and updated daily; Table 1 reads it, not Melee. Every public list, the standings and every round count (byes left out). Melee numbers its playoff rounds like Swiss ones, so a top 8 is marked when the last three rounds are a quarterfinal, semifinal and final among the top eight. A deck's record is its paper record (TopDeck.gg and Melee) when it has one, else its Magic Online top-32 record.

come from the same three sources as the other formats. Some paper events are listed as Vintage when they're really 7-point Highlander or Commander, where nearly every card is a single copy; events where half or more of the decks are like that are left out, in every format but Canadian Highlander.

isn't played on Magic Online, so it comes from TopDeck.gg alone, from 16 players up (its events are smaller), and its screens say "Results from TopDeck.gg". Its events are small, so most windows say the numbers rest on few events.

Decks are named by rules for each format's known archetypes. Canadian Highlander decks are singletons that share few cards, so they're named by their colors and plan (Esper Control, Bant Midrange, Red Deck Wins, Jeskai Black), and a color pair or shard's own name (Izzet, Naya) for the rarer ones. New groups of decks are named by Claude and checked by a person before they show.

Limited: 17Lands' public data, credited on every Limited screen. Its files come out about two weeks after a set reaches Arena, then keep updating. Each cube run's data is from that run; when 17Lands publishes a new file for a cube, Table 1 reads its first rows to tell whether it's the same run updated or a new one.
No player names, anywhere.
Every view opens with two or three short sentences, written by Claude from that view's numbers: what moved, and one deck, card or pair worth knowing.

Every card printed for paper play (about 37,900 cards and 110,000 printings) is downloaded once as a compact card file and kept on your device, so search, browsing, deck pages, stats and the scanner work offline and instantly. It refreshes daily from Scryfall but downloads again only when the cards actually change. The file also carries each card's printed names in ten other languages, legality, Canadian Highlander points, the mana each card makes, the tokens it creates, and each printing's illustrator and frame, for the scanner.

entries.t: New sets the hour they appear
entries.x: Scryfall's set list is read every hour, and a set released in the last month or the next two whose card count grew is read card by card straight away, then the card file is rebuilt (at most every two hours). The nightly update still brings everything else.
by name: exact matches first, then names that start with what you typed, then any match; tokens last. Add cards searches also take Scryfall's syntax (see Advanced search).

a deck, cube, binder, all your binders and Wants each have their own search. Every word must appear in the card's name or type line, so "jace mind" finds Jace, the Mind Sculptor and "legendary creature" finds legends.
loads at the smallest size that looks sharp, with rounded corners at the real card proportion, including Alpha's rounder corners and the square Collectors' Edition.
Wherever you add a card it starts as the card's original paper printing, for example Alpha Lightning Bolt rather than a promo. You can change it any time.
foil copies show a light rainbow shimmer over the card image, etched copies a dimmer one, wherever the finish is known.

USD is TCGplayer's market price and EUR is Cardmarket's, both via Scryfall, daily. Those are near-mint prices. A copy's price follows its condition: NM 100%, LP 90%, MP 75%, HP 60%, DMG 40% of the near-mint price, rounded to the cent. Your collection's value, All cards, card pages, binders, trades, trade matches and the import preview price each copy in its condition. Decks, cubes, wants, search results and Stats have no condition and show near mint. (Scryfall publishes no prices by condition, so these are fixed discounts.)

a card's price in dollars is Cardmarket's converted at the European Central Bank's daily rate (non-foil and foil; etched never), refreshed nightly. A card's page marks it "≈ $7,992.55 · from Cardmarket". A converted price under a tenth of the card's cheapest TCGplayer price is left out, since a few Cardmarket prices point at the wrong product. Collection value, trades, trade matches and the redraft pile use it; want prices and price alerts stay on TCGplayer only.
at the top: up to two of its hero cards' art side by side (or, without heroes, your most valuable cards), with how many cards you have and what they're worth. Tap it for All cards.

a row each that you swipe sideways. Each tile shows its hero card's art (or the card it holds most of), its name, and for decks the format. The arrow beside the heading opens the full list, with New deck, New binder or New cube. With none yet, the row offers to make one.

decks, binders and cubes come after your own on their row, with the owner's name and "N new" in teal when they've changed, and their art: the owner's hero card, else the card it holds most of that isn't a basic land. Tap one to open it. (The full Following list opens from a follow notification, or from the sidebar on a computer.)
at the top: Add cards, New deck, New binder or New cube.

(iPhone and Android): scan a pile of cards, then Add puts them all in your collection, a deck, a cube, a binder, your wants or a trade (see Card scanning). What it added shows under the bar with Undo.
(the magnifier): search every card by name or with Scryfall syntax. Each result shows how many copies you own, and a tap opens its card page, where you can add it anywhere.

entries.t: Search finds decks, cubes and binders
entries.x: from two letters, Decks, Cubes and Binders sections sit above the cards. Yours come first, matched on the device by every word of the search in the name or format (so they show offline). Then everyone else's you can see: decks, cubes and binders you follow (on the owner's profile or through the link you followed), friends' shared ones, and anyone's set to Anyone on a public profile, matched by name, owner's name or format; followed first, then friends', people you've played with, everyone else. Each row reads "Deck · Modern · Mara Quinn" (yours without a name, binders "Binder · For trade") with its card count; three per kind, then Show all N. Never your own twice, nothing private, nothing across a block.

a card's name (three letters or more; basic lands left out) also finds the decks, cubes and binders that hold it, everyone else's you can see and your own, with how many ("Deck · Modern · Mara Quinn · 4 Lightning Bolt"). Archetypes lists the Insights archetypes in the formats it reads whose name or format matches, most played first, with their tournament lists in the last 90 days; a tap opens the archetype's page. Rankings lists the cube and set rankings you can see (yours first, then friends'), by the cube or set, who ranked it or its label; a tap opens the ranking. Accounts a moderator has restricted don't show.
along the bottom open Trades (with your trade matches), Wants, and Import and export.

Each copy is tracked by printing, finish (non-foil, foil, etched), condition and language. Two foil and three non-foil copies of the same printing are separate counts, as are copies of other printings.

lists every card you own, grouped by card ("Lightning Bolt · 3 printings · 7 copies"), as a list, a grid or stacks. Sort by Recent, Price (most valuable single copy first, in its condition; cards with no price yet come first, so they're easy to look up), Name, MV or Set.

(View menu, every card list): Sort by name (A to Z), Sort by mana value (spells from lowest to highest, then lands, each by name) or Sort by set (newest set first, then collector number; the printing that counts is the one shown, and a card too new for the card data goes last). Binders also have Most copies first, where they start; All cards also has Recent and Price, and its row picks the same setting. Decks, cubes and shared sections start on Name. Each kind of screen remembers its own choice on the device; decks and cubes share theirs with ones a friend shares.
(View menu): split All cards or a binder into groups by type, color, color identity or mana value, or show them ungrouped. The sort applies inside each group, and in stacks each group is one stack.

each combination is its own group, in this order: White, Blue, Black, Red, Green; the pairs Azorius, Dimir, Rakdos, Gruul, Selesnya, Orzhov, Izzet, Golgari, Boros, Simic; the three-color Esper, Grixis, Jund, Naya, Bant, Abzan, Jeskai, Sultai, Mardu, Temur; the four-color Not white, Not blue, Not black, Not red, Not green; Five-color; Colorless. Headings of two colors or more show the letters ("Azorius · WU"). A card's identity is Scryfall's: mana symbols in its rules text count, so Golos is Five-color. Lands have no group of their own here: Breeding Pool is Simic, a Mountain Red, Command Tower and fetch lands Colorless.

a card you own in several printings or finishes is one row with a chevron; open it to see each printing and finish with its count and price. View → Expand all printings opens every card. Lists start collapsed each visit.

Tap any card (in All cards, a deck, a cube, a binder, your wants, a friend's profile or a shared link) and its page opens: the card as large as the screen allows, one row under it, and one bar at the bottom. The bar's price is the version on screen in its finish and condition.

Set (a grid of every printing, earliest first), Language, Condition (NM, LP, MP, HP, DMG) and Finish (only the finishes the printing has, and hidden when it has one). When your copies differ it reads MIX. A non-English printing's language is its own.

On a card you own, picking another set, language, condition or finish changes the copies on screen, each staying in its binder. With several copies it asks One copy or All; with several different versions it asks before changing them all. Undo puts them back. Changing the set keeps the finish if the new printing has it.

− count + for the copies on screen. + adds one more of that version, − takes one away; at 0 the page keeps that version so + puts it back. New cards start as the card's original printing, in the condition and language you last added in.

own it in more than one printing, finish, condition or language and they show two across, each with its count. Tap one to select it (an outline in teal): the row then shows and changes only that one, and − count + count and change that version's copies. Tap it again to go back to all of them.

hold + (on a computer, hold or right-click it). A copy of the version on screen (the selected one, or the one you have most of) appears as its own card, dimmed and selected, with a count of one; nothing is added yet. Change its set, language, condition or finish (in a deck or cube: set, language, finish or section). While it matches a version you already have it stays dimmed; the first change that makes it new adds it, in the binder or section you're in, with Undo. Before that, − and + set how many it will add, − at one drops it, and leaving the page drops it too.

from a deck or cube the page counts that list's copies and its row is Set, Finish and Section (Main, Sideboard, Considering): no Language or Condition there, even when the deck records one; from a binder it counts and changes that binder's copies. From All cards, Add cards or a link it's your whole collection.

(from a deck or cube): when you own the card in printings or finishes the list doesn't name, a strip over the row reads "You own N in other printings · Match collection", and the details have the same row. It opens a grid of every version you own (printing and finish, all conditions and languages together), two across, each with "Own N" and how many are picked in teal. It starts filled in: the versions the list already uses, then the ones you hold most of. Tap a tile for one more of it; once you've picked all you own of it, or every copy the list needs, a tap puts it back to none. Clear and Auto start over; a card in more than one section picks the section first. Use these printings changes the list's copies to your picks in one edit (each keeps its language, copies not picked stay as they are) with Undo; with nothing to change it reads Already matches.

with more than one copy on screen, the + at the top asks One copy or All N copies first. With a version selected it's that version's copies; otherwise All adds every version on screen with its count, to whichever place you pick next.

the + at the top (or the bottom bar, on a card from your wants, Missing, a friend or a shared link) adds the copies you chose (one, from the bottom bar) to your Collection, a Deck (then Main deck, Sideboard or Considering), a Cube, a Binder, your Wants (any printing, this printing, or this printing and finish) or a Trade (an open one or a new one, as a get, or a give when you own it). Undo works for collection, binder, deck and cube adds.

(the list icon): the rules text (read from Scryfall when you open it; it needs a connection), price (in the copy's condition, with near mint beside it when it isn't NM: "$9.00 · LP (NM $10.00)"), type, mana cost, rarity, artist and printing. Under them: Add to collection when opened from a deck or cube, which decks and cubes use the card (warning when they ask for more than you own), your copies with where they are and Move, Add to wants, Make it a hero, and the history of the printing on screen.
Double-faced cards have Flip under the card; tap the card to zoom in on it.
search the catalog by name or with Scryfall syntax, or scan with the camera (phones).
Binders say where your copies are; wants say what you're after. Both sync to every device and feed trades and trade matches.
Make up to 200, named as you like. A binder holds some of your copies; the rest are Unsorted.
Mark a binder For trade: its copies are what trades give first and what friends can match.
When copies leave your collection, they come out of Unsorted first, then binders not for trade, then for-trade binders.

in a binder: Move in a copy you own elsewhere (Unsorted first), or + New to add one straight into the binder. Scan adds the cards you scan, new, straight into the binder as one batch. Undo any of them.
shows a binder's cards as a list, a grid or stacks, and can expand every card's printings.
Deleting a binder puts its copies back in Unsorted.
Want a card in any printing, a printing, or a printing in one finish, with a quantity and an optional max price.
The printing picker lists every printing with rarity, year, language and price, and filters by set, number or year when there are many.
Your max price is never shown to anyone else; it only flags matches "over your max" for you.
can scan: each card you scan is wanted once, any printing (phones).

each want shows its near-mint price (Now $12.40 for a printing, From $3.20 for any printing: the cheapest English printing and finish), and under it the change over the last 7 days: "▼ 8% this week" (in teal), "▲ 12% this week" or "Flat this week". While a card has less than a week of history it says "since yesterday" or "in 3 days". Moves under 5 cents count as flat.

Worked out, never stored: every card your decks and cubes ask for more copies of than you own, in any printing, one line per card with the largest shortfall and the lists that need it. Shown in the printing the list that needs most names.
everyone has basics, so a deck's Islands are never missing, even if your collection has none. A want you add for a basic yourself still shows.
One tap adds a Missing card to your wants.

In a trade, cards you get that meet a want or a Missing line (in any printing of the card) are highlighted ("Want", "Missing · Burn"), and confirming the trade takes them off your wants. Undo puts them back.

decks and cubes (a Buy row under Add to collection, "12 to buy · $83.40"), Wants and Missing all open one screen before TCGplayer: the total large with "60 cards · 48 owned · 12 to buy"; Skip cards I own (decks and cubes, on to start, basic lands left out while on), Any printing I own counts (on: any printing, finish or language of the card covers a line, its own printing first; off: only that printing and finish), Exact printings (off: one Mass Entry cart by name; on: each printing on its own product page; on to start for Wants), Tokens (decks, off to start: the tokens the main deck, commander and sideboard make, one each in their catalog printing, always on their own pages) and Boards (decks: command zone, main deck and sideboard on to start, Considering off). Then the cards to buy by board ("Main deck · 12 to buy · 48 owned"), each with its count and "Own 2 of 4" when you have some (a tap opens the card), Price (every listed copy at its printing's near-mint market price), Owned (minus the copies you own) and Total, and Buy on TCGplayer along the bottom, which opens the cart or the menu of links as below. The options are remembered on the device for decks, cubes, Wants and Missing separately.
Add to → TCGplayer on any card's page opens the version on screen (one copy or all) on its TCGplayer product page; a printing TCGplayer has no page for goes into Mass Entry by name.

(on Wants) puts every want for any printing into TCGplayer's Mass Entry, the right count of each card by name, and opens a want for a specific printing on that printing's own TCGplayer product page. With more than one link a menu lists them: Mass Entry first, then each printing with its count. Buy missing on TCGplayer (above Missing from decks and cubes) does the same for what your decks and cubes are short.

It opens in your browser, so TCGplayer's sign-in and cart are your own. There, pick Normal or Foil and a condition for the list, tap Add to Cart, then Optimize on the cart to find the cheapest mix of sellers. TCGplayer doesn't let another app start the optimizer, so that tap is yours.
A very long list comes in parts ("Part 1 of 3"), each adding to the same cart: tap Buy again for the next part.
Prices on TCGplayer are its live listings, so they can differ from the market price your wants show.

the links go through Table 1's TCGplayer affiliate link, which sends you on to the same page; buying from it earns Table 1 a commission at no cost to you. The link names only the app (iPhone, Android or website) and the screen (a deck, a cube, a card, Wants or Missing), never you.

Once a day (late afternoon in Europe, midday in the US) you get one notification listing the wants that got cheaper: "Counterspell is $7.50, 25% under its 30-day average." or "Lightning Bolt is $1.40, under your max of $1.50. Also cheaper: Opt and Ponder." Tapping it opens Wants.

means at least 15% and at least $1 under the want's average over the last 30 days (it needs a week of prices first). Each want alerts at most once a week, and after that only when it's 5% lower than the price it last alerted at, so a card that stays low doesn't repeat.
a want with a max alerts when its price falls to it or below, once; it can alert again only after the price has gone back over the max.
